sentences.text: This is the first application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed by the applicant for grant of bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text:
The applicant has been implicated in connection with Crime No.512/2022, registered at Police Station, Barghat, District - Seoni (M.P.) for commission of offences punishable under Sections 376,
376(3), 376(2)(cha) of IPC and Section 5n & of POCSO Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 12.10.2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: As per prosecution case, the allegation against the present applicant is that on 06.04.2022 took the prosecutrix at his home and committed rape upon her, due to which she became pregnant.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Accordingly, a case has been registered against the present applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the alleged offence due to old enmity between parties.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Applicant is only 24 years old.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: The FIR was lodged after a delay of more than 05 months and there is no plausible explanation has been assigned for the aforesaid delay.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is further submitted that, as per the DNA report, applicant is not the biological father of the newly born child.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 12.10.2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Conclusion of trial will take considerable long time.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, he prays for grant of bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned Deputy Government Advocate for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer and prays for its rejection.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text:
After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact as per DNA report, applicant is not the biological father of the newly born child; therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for securing his presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023.json

sentences.text:
It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial, but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.
The M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
Certified Copy, as per rules.
(RAJENDRA KUMAR (VERMA)) JUDGE Amitabh Abhishek vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117254211/

opennyai_summary.21_February_2023__facts:
This is the first application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed by the applicant for grant of bail.
The applicant has been implicated in connection with Crime No.512/2022, registered at Police Station, Barghat, District - Seoni (M.P.) for commission of offences punishable under Sections 376,
376(3), 376(2)(cha) of IPC and Section 5n & of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 12.10.2022.
As per prosecution case, the allegation against the present applicant is that on 06.04.2022 took the prosecutrix at his home and committed rape upon her, due to which she became pregnant.
Accordingly, a case has been registered against the present applicant.
opennyai_summary.21_February_2023__decision:
Investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.
The applicant is in custody since 12.10.2022.
Conclusion of trial will take considerable long time.
It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for securing his presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during trial.
opennyai_summary.21_February_2023__ANALYSIS:
After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact as per DNA report, applicant is not the biological father of the newly born child; therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.

opennyai_summary.10_January_2025__facts:
The applicant is in judicial custody since 10.11.2023.
On such statements, prosecution for offences punishable under Sections 366,
366A, 376(2)(n) and 376(3) of IPC and 3/4 and 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act was added.
opennyai_summary.10_January_2025__arguments:
No offence, as alleged, is committed by the applicant.
It is a case of teenage romance between two young adolescents.
Victim had left her parental home at her own will.
Victim had informed that she is major.
He is a labourer by profession.
There is no likelihood of absconsion leaving his family, home and profession.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
The trial would take time to complete.
Therefore, the applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
opennyai_summary.10_January_2025__ANALYSIS: There is no likelihood of tampering with the evidence by the applicant.
opennyai_summary.10_January_2025__decision:
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:779 3 MCRC-54996-2024 circumstances of the case, having regard to the young age of the applicant, without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
Accordingly, it is directed that applicant- Abhishek S/o Budhiya Mankar shall be released on bail in connection with the Crime as stated in para - 1 of this order, upon furnishing personal bond and surety bond of amount, as may be considered appropriate by the Trial Court/the Committal Court for compliance with conditions, as may be imposed by such Court, to secure presence of the applicant for the trial under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C., 1973/Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial.
However, in case of breach of any of the preconditions of bail, the concerned Court may consider, on merit, cancellation of bail without any impediment of this order.
The concerned Court shall get the conditions reproduced on the personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.
If any of them is unable to write, the scribe shall certify that he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused or the surety.
C.C. as per rules
